notes:
Hermes runs a GENUINE autonomous self-prompting loop (/goal, hermes_cli/goals.py) whose iteration cap is real configuration — goals.max_turns in $HERMES_HOME/config.yaml — so this cell records the actual cap-hit rather than claudecode's /goal clear stand-in. With max_turns=2 the loop fires exactly two turns: the /goal kickoff enqueues the goal text itself, the judge returns continue and hermes self-prompts a second turn, then turns_used>=max_turns flips the goal to paused with no continuation prompt. The distinguishing assertion is iter2_start: it must go ready→working with NO driver-sent input between the two wait_turns, which is what makes this a self-prompting loop and not an externally-fed one. The termination assertion is cap_reached_dwell: after the second working→ready the session settles and DWELLS in ready with no further working transition — the loop stopped at its limit and did not stick in working or spuriously re-prompt. Presession form: hermes' sessions row is INSERTed ~2s after launch while the process exists from launch, so a transient proc-<PID> row is born first and reconciles into the store-keyed id; every post-birth phase anchors to the real session. No waiting is ever expected — the goal needs no tool approval.

RECORD-TIME FINDINGS (2026-08-03, recording 2-8 on daemon 21fd275, coexist daemon on :7838): 8/8 phases green on the SECOND take.
(1) THE FIRST TAKE ENDED FOR THE WRONG REASON, and that is the finding worth carrying. The assessed recipe used an impossible goal ("reply with one integer that is simultaneously odd and even"), assuming an unsatisfiable goal keeps the judge returning `continue` until the turn budget stops the loop. The live judge (auxiliary.goal_judge at its default provider: auto, i.e. gpt-5.6-luna) returned verdict=done after ONE turn: "The agent correctly explains that no integer can be both odd and even under standard definitions, making the requested goal impossible" (persisted at state_meta key goal:20260803_010132_187bae, status=done, turns_used=1, max_turns=2). Every state phase except the dwell would have looked plausible while the cell recorded GOAL COMPLETION rather than the iteration cap. The goal is now a long, objectively incomplete task (write 1..2000 in blocks of 100) so `done` is unavailable inside two turns.
(2) THE CAP IS RECORDED, AND ITS FALSIFIER IS CHECKED. Second take: state_meta goal:20260803_010756_4c63dd ends status=paused, paused_reason="turn budget exhausted (2/2)", turns_used=2, max_turns=2, last_verdict=continue - the judge still wanted to continue and the BUDGET stopped it. Arc on the one store-backed session 20260803_010756_4c63dd: ready(01:08:01.74) -> working(.78) -> ready(01:08:09.68) -> working(01:08:13.40) -> ready(01:08:17.20), then a flat ready dwell through the trailing sleep with no working and no waiting. Iteration 2 opens with a "[Continuing toward your standing goal]" user row the driver never typed, and iteration 3 never starts - which is the whole cell.
(3) THE max_turns=2 CAP IS NOW APPLIED BY THE DRIVER, not by hand. The assessment recorded that the driver accepts SETTINGS_PATH but never reads it, so the recording setup had to write goals.max_turns into <HERMES_HOME>/config.yaml out of band. Driver commit ac01f1e7 fixes that: apply_settings deep-merges the recipe's settings blob into config.yaml before launch and the cleanup trap restores it. Verified on this run - the driver logged the merge, and config.yaml was byte-identical (same md5) before and after.
(4) THE goal_judge PRECONDITION WAS DROPPED, with evidence rather than by assumption. The assessment required auxiliary.goal_judge be re-pointed at a model returning strict JSON, else the parse-failure auto-pause (3 consecutive non-JSON verdicts, goals.py:1560) would end the loop for the wrong reason. On this install it is unnecessary: across the 2.7 and 2.8 recordings the default judge produced five usable verdicts and consecutive_parse_failures stayed 0 in both persisted goal states. Re-check if the recording home's model.default changes.
(5) tokens_nonzero STRIPPED, model PINNED in its place - the standing hermes-column trade (1-6, 2-1, 2-7, 2-10, 2-13, 3-2, 3-5). SEEN RED on this recording: "observations: FAIL - tokens: want >0 got 0" with 8/8 state phases green. Structural, not drift: `of verify` asserts against the REPLAY GOLDEN summary, produced by driving core/pkg/tailer with hermes.Parser (ModelName only), while hermes' token aggregate lives on the `sessions` row and reaches irrlicht only through ComputeMetrics, a path replay never runs. Unlock = extend the #766 golden lift + StageReplayStore to hermes as #775/#776 did for antigravity.
source: .specs/agent-scenarios.md → Feature: Autonomous loop iteration limit reached

text: Pre-session (proc-<PID>) appears in ready within 1s of launching hermes chat
The store-keyed session reconciles in with a DIFFERENT session_id once hermes INSERTs its sessions row on the first message, born ready
PID bound to the store-keyed session
Loop start: /goal <unsatisfiable> sets the goal and immediately enqueues it, driving ready → working
First iteration ends on finish_reason='stop' → working → ready. The judge cannot mark the impossible goal done, so the loop continues; turns_used=1 of 2.

Second iteration begins with NO user input from the driver — hermes self-prompts its own continuation prompt back into the input queue. This is the assertion that distinguishes an autonomous loop from an externally-fed one.
Second iteration ends → working → ready. turns_used=2 reaches max_turns=2, so the goal flips to paused with no continuation prompt: this is the cap-hit.

Spec: state reaches ready even though the agent did not succeed, and does not stick in working. With the turn budget exhausted the loop stops self-prompting entirely — no further messages row is written — so the session dwells in ready for at least 15s with no post-cap working transition and never any waiting.
